notes: All three levels use one shared MetricSelection component. Six cards show large icons and short names. Official full names remain accessible button labels; a selected definition appears once in the tray. One or three physical slots support keyboard selection, review and removal; Level 1 permits direct replacement and Levels 2/3 retain the three-choice limit.

A 420ms card flight and slot arrival provide normal-motion feedback without delaying the primary action. Reduced motion fills the slot immediately. Transient flights clean up after completion and unmount. Tablet layouts place the tray above the cards; phone slots use complete horizontal rows to avoid broken words. All 1366/768/390/320px choices passed and screenshots were reviewed.

Repeated action-footer captions are removed in every chapter, including Choose 1 of 6, selection summaries, evaluation-ready text and cover-six instructions. Necessary choice-limit feedback lives beside the slots. Replay scene and Reset weights remain controls. Obsolete per-level choice styles and the replaced MetricChecklist component were removed.

Classroom observations pair an illustrated notebook with a quieter fact and stronger behavioural consequence. Level 1 preserves its original evidence. Level 2 uses shorter two-part copy for visible, quality and mixed branches, all-six and final observations. The notebook marks the actual tracked categories and leaves other categories outside it; full six-area coverage removes the outside group.

Level 2 core reports use short metric names and icon/check cards. Its 10/25/100 expansions fill the real checkbox field and gain decorative paper layers. Checklist actions still reveal and tick in order. No duplicate checklist was added to three/six-metric evaluation dashboards.

Level 3 results and every comparison record include an Alex desk vignette driven by the existing effort category: rapid work and extra papers for intense effort, ordinary work for steady effort, relaxed posture with a checked sheet for minimum effort. Weight numbers are secondary and no numerical effort or learning score was invented. Vignettes reveal with observed rows after manual Observe, not during weight editing/publication.

All 20 Level 3 trios, adaptive routes, inclusive 10-point near-even boundaries, linked final-pair confirmation, freely changed second tests, exact actual snapshots, partner scene IDs, name/sound/trio handoffs, real-time audio, hidden-page holds and fresh-session behaviour passed. All 25 authored emoji remain distinct and Alex retains two short workbench replies. The added visual suite also verifies all three Level 2 evidence branches.

The shared satisfaction report milestones and chapter baselines remain unchanged. Reports raise the bar once; choosing/resetting/replaying/comparing does not. Near-even weights earn no bonus. There is no player Restart, administrator login or Design Lab transition. Partner cinematic assets remain replaceable placeholders, ending at the final theory frame.

All four individual/combined entries and the two-version review ZIP were rebuilt from the same source. Release checks verified actual ZIP contents, byte equality and hashes and played through all three connected chapters. Version-numbered historical archives and earlier validation reports remain unchanged.

Managed Chromium serves exact offline production HTML bytes through an in-memory HTTPS origin because local file navigation is blocked. Direct file opening in the user browser, classroom load capacity and finished partner videos were not tested.
